newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean metals futures and options trade surges.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean metals futures and options trade surges.

text.p: South Korea's trade in base metals futures and options surged in the first quarter of this year, which brokers said on Tuesday was due to heavy trading by a large local dealer on the London Metal Exchange (LME).

According to data from the Korea Futures Association, the country's base metal futures trade volume surged to 364,713 lots between January-March from 30,892 lots in the same year ago period. In 1996, base metal futures trade totalled 503,553 lots.
All of South Korea's metal futures transactions are conducted on overseas exchanges, including the LME and the Commodity Exchange in New York.
An official at the Ministry of Finance and Economy said the increased trade volume was due to a combination of rising metals options trade and a change in statistical reporting procedure.

"We did not count metal options trade volume early last year, but we started including the options trade volume with the futures volume from the second half of last year as the options trade volume began to increase," the ministry official said.
Brokers said South Korea's LG Metals Corp had been increasing its activity in LME options business over the past year.

Last week London traders said a Korean firm's unwinding of short copper option positions had pushed up volatilities and its granting of aluminium options had depressed aluminium volatilities on the LME.
LG Metal officials were not immediately available for comment on the reports. The company is part of the LG Group and is South Korea's largest copper producer.

The London traders said on Friday nearby upside copper options were purchased as cover by the company which had been prominent in the market at the end of last year and early 1997 for granting large lumps of copper and aluminium options.
They said the firm has been running a short ledger and was caught out by the recent rise in LME prices, which hit last week a fresh one-year peak of $2,530, basis three-months, they said.
Traders said they were not sure whether the company was unwinding its existing positions or carrying forward.
However, they said they recalled that LG Metals had been rumoured in late January to have been caught in a "short" position by a European merchant going "long."
The company had been rumoured to have run large copper short positions totalling 100,000 to 200,000 tonnes on the LME.
